meta.purpose: Independent, line-by-line re-derivation of every headline number the live site publishes, plus an irregularity register. Imports nothing from scripts/ or pipeline/.
meta.caveat: Reproducibility is not validation. These checks show the published numbers follow from the committed extract. They say nothing about whether any strategy is profitable or any price obtainable.

checks.claim: Pearson r: QB passing yards vs WR1 receiving yards (same team-game)
checks.note: Reconstructed with this module's own QB/WR1 rule on regular-season team-games only. The published r differs by 0.002 (0.5616 vs 0.5602) because the published population also includes POST-season team-games.

checks.claim: Team-games behind that correlation (published) vs regular-season-only recomputation
checks.note: The published n=7560 counts POST-season team-games too; this module's REG-only population is 6024, and the extract holds 266 POST team-game groups, which accounts for the difference. The correlation coefficient agrees to three decimals either way.

Near zero means the deviation was noise, not skill.

irregularities.title: The 50.0% ATS coin-flip test is a tautology, not evidence
irregularities.detail: data/derived/luck.json reports n=13,784 and wins=6,892. 13,784 = 2 x 6,892: every game contributes one cover by the home side and one by the away side, so a pooled per-team-game cover rate is 50% by construction and the reported binomial p of 1.0 carries no information. The real, testable rate is the home-side cover rate, which the same extract puts at 0.4891 (3,371 of 6,892 decided games, two-sided p=0.073, normal approximation with continuity correction because n is 6,892).
irregularities.impact: The site's 'the spread market shows no exploitable tilt' conclusion survives, but the quoted statistic behind it does not measure what it claims. Treat the p=1.0 as unverified.

irregularities.title: Two different 'our model' MAE numbers are published on different pages
irregularities.detail: README.md states the model spread MAE is 10.38 vs market 9.70; index.html and pages/lines.html state 10.391 vs 9.711. This module recomputes 10.391 vs 9.711 from data/derived/predictions.csv, which matches the site.
irregularities.impact: README prose is stale against the committed data. The site is correct; the README should be updated by its owner.

irregularities.title: Committed data ends before the week the site is being read in
irregularities.detail: The schedules extract's latest gameday is 2026-11-01. The official NFL injury report for 2026 Week 10 (games of 12-15 November 2026) is already published, and its team records differ from the extract (e.g. the report shows NYG 5-2-1 and WAS 2-5-1; the extract, through 2026-11-01, resolves to NYG 4-2-1 and WAS 2-4-1 by its own convention). Any 'current slate' claim on the site is a snapshot, not live.
irregularities.impact: Line origination for an unplayed week cannot be scored or compared to market using this extract. The pipeline must refresh before any decision that depends on this week.
irregularities.source_text: NFL.com official injury report, 2026 Week 10 - records printed on the page

irregularities.title: Ties are silently excluded from the Pythagorean win totals
irregularities.detail: 16 regular-season games in the extract ended in a tie. The expected-wins model that produces the published R^2 counts only wins and losses (wins = count(margin > 0)), so tied games are scored as losses in the denominator but never as results. That does not change the headline conclusion but it does bias the luck decomposition by a few hundredths of a win per team-season.
irregularities.impact: Minor. Document the convention before the luck decomposition is used to rank anything.

irregularities.title: No historical player-prop prices exist in any committed source
irregularities.detail: data/derived/props.json evaluates prop *accuracy* (MAE) against realised box scores. There is no committed file containing a historical over/under price for a player prop, so no prop ROI, edge, or parlay price for props can be computed, and none should be displayed. The site says this; the leaderboard still lists 'player prop combos' as a family, which reads as if it had been tested.
irregularities.impact: Any prop-family strategy must remain 'no price -> no result' until a licensed price source is committed.
irregularities.source_text: nflverse stats_player release - box scores only, no prices

irregularities.title: Injury, depth-chart and snap-count feeds are published upstream but not committed here
irregularities.detail: nflverse publishes `injuries_{season}`, `depth_charts_{season}` and `snap_counts_{season}` release assets for every season from 2015 to 2026. None of them is in this repository, and the sandbox this session runs in can reach only github.com/api.github.com, and the release assets themselves redirect to a host that is blocked, so the files cannot be ingested here. Every injury/depth claim in this repository is therefore either a description of the official report (checked by hand) or unverified.
irregularities.impact: The injury and backup-depth requirement cannot be met from inside this environment. It needs a workflow run on GitHub-hosted runners that downloads those assets and commits the derived summaries, exactly as the existing data-pipeline does for schedules.

irregularities.title: Gate G1 (point-in-time integrity) cannot be satisfied by the current feeds
irregularities.detail: G1 reads: 'Inputs are strictly pre-kickoff; no result-derived feature; source hashes recorded.'. The schedules extract carries a single `spread_line` per game with no timestamp saying when it was captured, and the injury/depth feeds that would date a lineup are not committed (IR-06). So the only point-in-time claim the pipeline can actually evidence is 'the line in the file'.
irregularities.impact: Before any strategy is funded, the project needs a timestamped line capture and a timestamped lineup snapshot. No amount of modelling substitutes for that.

irregularities.title: Unfinished seasons are treated as complete team-seasons in the luck decomposition
irregularities.detail: The Pythagorean/luck table keeps every team with gp >= 8, which includes 2 partial team-seasons from the in-progress 2026 season (through 2026-11-01). Their expected wins are pro-rated by games played, so they do not bias the mean, but they do inflate the spread of actual win% and therefore move the reported R^2: with win% (published definition) it is 0.8191; if raw wins are used instead it is 0.8300. The published R^2 also uses win% while the persistence test uses raw luck wins, so the two rows of the luck table are not on the same scale.
irregularities.impact: Report the luck decomposition on completed seasons only, or label 2026 as partial. The direction of every conclusion (luck does not persist) is unchanged.
irregularities.source_text: nflverse schedules - max gameday among played games = 2026-11-01

irregularities.title: A cited official URL returns 404 (rulebook path changed)
irregularities.detail: This session initially cited https://operations.nfl.com/the-rules/2026-nfl-rulebook/ for game-settlement context. That path returns the NFL's 404 page. The live path is https://operations.nfl.com/rules-officiating/2026-nfl-rulebook, which returns the 2026 rulebook and lists the four 2026 rule changes (6-1-3, 6-1-5, 6-1-6, 19-2). An earlier session already logged a 404 on the 2025 equivalent (IR/FL-09 in its register), so this is a recurring class of error in this repository, not a one-off.
irregularities.impact: Every rulebook citation in the repository should be re-checked. A citation that 404s is not evidence, and the settlement rules (push, overtime, final score) matter for any backtest that uses them.
irregularities.source_text: NFL Football Operations - 2026 NFL Rulebook (live path verified 2026-11-12)

irregularities.title: The NFL's injury-report policy page returns no article body
irregularities.detail: https://operations.nfl.com/football-ops/league-governance/injury-report/ returns the NFL 404 page, and the long-standing policy PDF at https://operations.nfl.com/media/2683/2017-nfl-injury-report-policy.pdf returns an empty document to this session's retrieval tool. The reporting deadlines quoted on the injury page therefore come from the official 2026-27 league calendar (which states the practice-report and game-status-report filing days), not from the policy document itself.
irregularities.impact: The deadline facts are still officially sourced. The policy's own wording about what must be disclosed is quoted from second-hand summaries and is marked unverified.
irregularities.source_text: NFL 2026-27 important dates - filing deadlines for practice and game-status reports
